hypotheses.observation: Sequential elementwise multiply, add, subtract, and divide nodes materialize intermediate tensors.
hypotheses.mechanism: Intermediate materialization can add memory traffic and launch or scheduling overhead beyond the elementwise arithmetic itself.
hypotheses.transformation: Algebraically fuse compatible sequential elementwise operations into fewer elementwise stages, while preserving the original dependency order and numerical behavior.
preconditions: The expressions for new_v and new_state can be combined without changing required evaluation semantics.
The fused implementation supports compatible tensor shapes and division behavior.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Potential reduction in intermediate-memory traffic and execution overhead; magnitude is UNKNOWN because no profile is provided.
risks: Reassociation or changed operation ordering may violate forward or backward numerical equivalence.
Fusion may increase register pressure or reduce occupancy.
unknowns: Which graph nodes are actually dominant in runtime.
Whether the target GPU and compiler can efficiently fuse the resulting expression.
Whether gradients remain numerically equivalent after fusion.
required_evidence: A kernel or graph profile identifying materialization and launch costs.
Forward and backward numerical-equivalence results for the fused expression.

hypotheses.observation: Some coefficients are fixed across the invocation, while update expressions depend on beta, v, and old_v.
hypotheses.mechanism: Invariant coefficient handling may permit constant folding and lower runtime operand preparation or arithmetic overhead.
hypotheses.transformation: Precompute or fold invocation-invariant coefficients into the elementwise expression and eliminate redundant per-element coefficient work where algebraically valid.
preconditions: The coefficients remain unchanged for the full invocation.
Constant folding preserves the required forward and backward numerical equivalence.
The folded form does not introduce unacceptable precision changes.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Potential reduction in per-element arithmetic and parameter-loading overhead; actual benefit is UNKNOWN without profiling.
risks: Incorrectly treating a varying value as invariant would change results.
Precision or reassociation changes may fail numerical checks.
The optimization may be negligible if memory traffic dominates.
unknowns: The identities and data types of the fixed coefficients.
Whether coefficients are already folded by the existing compiler.
The relative cost of coefficient operations versus memory traffic.
required_evidence: A complete expression and coefficient-lifetime analysis.
Generated-kernel or graph inspection showing whether folding already occurs.
Forward and backward equivalence measurements after transformation.

hypotheses.observation: The state relation depends on old_state, old_v, new_v, and k, creating a dependency between the update and state computations.
hypotheses.mechanism: A producer-consumer fusion opportunity may avoid writing new_v to an intermediate tensor before consuming it in new_state.
hypotheses.transformation: Inline the computation of new_v into the new_state computation, or fuse the producer and consumer into one compatible elementwise kernel while retaining the dependency.
preconditions: new_v is consumed only in ways compatible with inlining or fusion.
The fused operation remains within acceptable resource limits.
Forward and backward numerical equivalence is verified.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Potential elimination of an intermediate write and read involving new_v, with possible reduction in memory traffic and execution overhead; runtime impact is UNKNOWN.
risks: Inlining may increase register usage and lower occupancy.
Changed evaluation order may alter numerical results.
Additional dependencies may prevent effective parallel scheduling.
unknowns: The size and lifetime of intermediate tensors.
The target kernel resource usage and achieved occupancy.
required_evidence: Kernel resource and memory-traffic profile before and after fusion.
